evals.prompt: I want to initialize a new GitHub repository for a modern frontend app called 'stellar-dashboard'. I want React with TypeScript and Vite, using pnpm as the package manager. For code quality, I want Biome and Lefthook for pre-commit hooks, with Conventional Commits. I also need complete GitHub Actions CI/CD for linting, testing, and building, Release Please for automated releases, and all governance files including README, MIT LICENSE, CONTRIBUTING.md, and SECURITY.md. We work in Trunk-Based mode and want Node 20 pinned via .node-version, plus Git Worktrees support for parallel agent development. Conduct the interview to confirm everything, synthesize the blueprint, wait for my approval, and then execute the setup cleanly.
evals.expected_output: The agent inspects the environment, conducts the decision interview, presents a clear Repository Blueprint with directory preview (including branching, worktrees, and DX files), waits for approval before executing scaffolding, generates valid configuration files (biome.json, lefthook.yml, ci.yml, release-please.yml, .node-version, scripts/worktree.sh, governance files), initializes git with a clean commit, and presents a completion report.
expectations: The agent does not create files or run destructive commands before presenting the blueprint and asking for confirmation.
The proposed blueprint includes React + TypeScript (Vite), pnpm, Biome, Lefthook, Conventional Commits, GitHub Actions CI, Release Please, .node-version, Git Worktrees, and governance files.
Generated configuration includes a valid biome.json, lefthook.yml, and .gitignore containing .worktrees/.
Generated .github/workflows directory contains ci.yml and release-please.yml.
Governance files include README.md, SECURITY.md, CONTRIBUTING.md (with branching and worktree sections), and LICENSE (MIT).
The git commit history contains a clean initial commit with conventional commit format (e.g. 'chore: initial repository bootstrap') without co-author mentions.

evals.prompt: Initialize a Python microservice repository named 'payment-webhook-service' using uv. We need Ruff for linting and formatting, Pytest for testing, multi-environment branches (main for prod, staging, develop), GitHub Actions CI on these branches, Dependabot for weekly updates, Python 3.11 pinned via .python-version, a setup.sh script, and full governance documentation (README, SECURITY.md, Apache 2.0 LICENSE). Ask me the necessary questions, propose the blueprint, and scaffold the repository.
evals.expected_output: The agent asks clarifying questions or confirms settled decisions, produces a structured blueprint showing multi-environment branches and setup scripts, waits for user approval, and generates pyproject.toml with uv/ruff configuration, .github/workflows/ci.yml with branch triggers, .github/dependabot.yml, .python-version, scripts/setup.sh, tests/ directory, and full documentation.
expectations: The agent presents a structured blueprint summarizing Python/uv, Ruff, Pytest, multi-environment branches, Dependabot, and Apache 2.0 license.
The agent stops at an approval gate before executing any scaffolding.
A pyproject.toml is generated containing [tool.ruff] configuration and dependency groups for dev (ruff, pytest).
.github/workflows/ci.yml triggers on main, staging, and develop branches.
A scripts/setup.sh and .python-version file are generated.
Governance files README.md, SECURITY.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, and Apache 2.0 LICENSE are generated.

evals.prompt: I want to create an agnostic repository called 'devops-playbooks' with no specific framework. I just need a clean structure with shell scripts, docker compose, Lefthook for pre-commit linting (shellcheck and markdownlint), Git Worktrees enabled with scripts/worktree.sh, GitHub Actions CI to validate scripts, and private repository creation on GitHub. Guide me through the interview and set it up.
evals.expected_output: The agent identifies the agnostic stack mode, asks any frontier questions, presents the blueprint for approval, scaffolds the directory layout with scripts/ and docs/, creates lefthook.yml, scripts/worktree.sh, ci.yml, governance files, and outlines the `gh repo create --private` command.
expectations: The agent recognizes the custom/agnostic mode and does not force an unwanted JS or Python framework.
The blueprint details the agnostic structure, Lefthook configuration, Git Worktrees workflow, CI workflow, and private GitHub repo intent.
The agent honors the approval gate before creating files.
Lefthook configuration includes hooks for shellcheck and markdownlint.
A worktree helper script scripts/worktree.sh is generated and .worktrees/ is ignored in .gitignore.
Git is initialized on the selected initial branch; the agent asks for a commit-message convention rather than assuming Conventional Commits.

evals.prompt: Initialize a repository that already has AGENTS.md requiring approval before commits and a local commit-generating skill that says commits may be created automatically. I have not chosen which rule should win. We do not use worktrees, and our commit messages follow an existing ticket-ID format rather than Conventional Commits. Show me the plan before changing anything.
evals.expected_output: The agent inspects and cites the actual accessible rules, surfaces the commit-approval conflict and asks the user to resolve it before changing affected governance. It preserves the chosen no-worktree and ticket-ID policies instead of generating mandatory worktree or Conventional Commits instructions.
expectations: The agent does not silently choose between AGENTS.md and the commit skill or assume a named skill exists without finding it.
The blueprint lists each material conflict with source, consequence, and a decision requested from the user.
The generated governance does not require worktrees or Conventional Commits when those policies were rejected.
No external skill or configuration is modified without specific approval.

evals.prompt: Bootstrap an existing GitHub repo on a dedicated branch. Its origin/main has advanced, but fetching origin now fails. I still want a worktree and a PR. Also, my local working tree contains unrelated changes. What do you do?
evals.expected_output: The agent reports that remote freshness is unverified, does not branch from a stale fallback, asks whether offline work is allowed, preserves unrelated changes, and defers push/PR until target divergence can be checked. It does not silently rebase or merge.
expectations: Fetch failure is visible and no fallback silently creates a worktree from an unverified branch.
Unrelated changes are not staged, committed, reset, or cleaned.
The agent does not claim the PR branch is current or publish it without target-branch verification and user authorization.

evals.prompt: Prepare an initialization blueprint for a new React/TypeScript Vite project using pnpm. I want lightweight fast tooling but have not chosen lint/format, hooks or release tooling. Read-only fixture: current official sources identify Oxlint as linter and Oxfmt as formatter; Biome and ESLint/Prettier are also candidates. Oxfmt quickstart documents oxfmt --check as non-writing, whereas bare oxfmt writes. Upstream publishes speed claims, but no comparable project benchmark exists. I need TSX, Markdown formatting, React rules and typechecking. Explain discovery, compare available options and stop before mutation. Do not invent evidence outside the fixture.
evals.expected_output: A contextual comparison including Oxlint/Oxfmt, Biome and ESLint/Prettier, with current discovery for all unresolved tools, compatibility checks and explicit evidence limitations, then a blueprint approval gate.
expectations: Includes Oxlint and Oxfmt as separate linter/formatter components alongside credible alternatives; no unconditional Biome or Oxc winner.
Checks actual file, rule/plugin, framework, type-aware and runtime compatibility; preserves separate typechecking.
Researches alternatives for hooks and release tools too, rather than only lint/format.
Does not present upstream speed/lightweight claims as observed project measurements.
Uses non-mutating lint/format-check scripts consistently for local checks and CI; does not use bare oxfmt as validation.
Stops before installation, file generation or GitHub mutation pending approval.

evals.prompt: Bootstrap CI and Release Please for an existing private organization GitHub repository. Read-only fixture: caller has write but not admin; repository Actions GET is allowed, workflow permissions GET returns 403, rulesets GET returns 404, and security_and_analysis is omitted. Org policy restricts actions; YAML contents/pull-requests write does not grant repository administration. Assess permissions and useful Git/GitHub options using CLI help and official API documentation without executing remote mutations or changing credentials. Show blueprint gaps and next actions.
evals.expected_output: A settings inventory covering relevant families and least privilege, explaining authorization vs workflow scopes, inherited restrictions and unknown evidence, with specific approval and readback gates.
expectations: Distinguishes caller access, Actions defaults/allow-list, workflow job token scopes and PR creation/approval setting.
Does not interpret 403, 404 or omitted security fields as disabled or confirmed unavailable.
Covers useful protections/rulesets, merge controls, access, security, environments and features; CLI create/edit flags are not presented as all options.
Preserves organization restrictions and least privilege; no credential scope escalation or broad write-all workaround.
Separates local files from remote changes, identifies blocked/deferred settings and requires approval for sensitive changes plus readback after approved mutations.

evals.prompt: Initialize missing governance in my local-only existing Vue/TypeScript project. pnpm lockfile and ESLint/Prettier configs already exist; custom ESLint plugin is required. I explicitly want to keep them. Network/registry research is unavailable. Do not ask stack/package-manager questions or migrate tooling. Explain what can be verified and propose only missing governance, with no execution before approval.
evals.expected_output: Preserve authoritative stack/package manager and explicit tooling choices; no remote permission administration or new tools forced; state research limitations and stop at approval.
expectations: Preserves pnpm and ESLint/Prettier without re-asking settled choices or imposing Oxlint/Oxfmt/Biome.
Marks current alternatives research unverified rather than claiming an exhaustive/current comparison.
Skips GitHub remote settings as not applicable while keeping relevant local Git discovery.
Does not install tools, migrate configs or create governance before blueprint approval.

evals.prompt: Engineering activation only in an existing repository for Codex and Claude Code. Preserve the current stack and Git governance. Recommend a selectable engineering kit; use the four-field question format. I have not yet approved source revision, installation or action permissions. Do not scaffold, install globally or ship changes.
evals.expected_output: Discover facts, ask unresolved choices in Current state / numbered Options / Recommendation / Response format, disclose dependencies and strict per-skill commands, present scoped blueprint and wait before mutations.
expectations: Engineering activation routes to the existing Repo Init owner, not mandatory scaffolding or a new CLI.
Only the four approved question fields appear, localized to the user.
Pins, selection, action permissions, conflicts and exact project destinations require approval.
No package execution, writes or shipping before applicable approval.

evals.prompt: Simulation only: the approved engineering kit is staged outside the target repository. CLAUDE.md points outside the project, one selected canonical skill has local edits, and skills-lock.json contains an unrelated installed skill. Do not execute network or Git mutations. Explain integration and recovery.
evals.expected_output: Block affected activation on external symlink/customized content, preserve unrelated lock entries and files, propose explicit conflict resolution rather than overwrite or global modification.
expectations: No external symlink target or customized skill is overwritten.
Staging and plan preserve unrelated lock entries and personal instructions.
No fallback copies, forced cleanup, silent adoption or global configuration changes.
A partial failure is reported as partial state, not atomic success or automatic rollback.

evals.prompt: Simulation only: source and installer are pinned and the unchanged project activation plan is approved. A global homonym remains model-invocable. Automated tests pass but neither Codex nor Claude Code was launched. I want a strict before-load confirmation gate. Explain what can be claimed without activating a real project.
evals.expected_output: Explain explicit-only adapters and separate activation per dependency, block strict-gate claim until homonym resolved, distinguish automated installation/configuration checks from unverified live host behavior.
expectations: Explicit per-skill user commands replace automatic chain handoffs.
Does not silently modify the global installation or treat passing tests as live host proof.
A global implicit-enabled homonym is a disclosed blocker for a strict project gate.
No merge/deployment executor is inferred from stored policy modes.
